sources.title: Yvonne Choquet-Bruhat, Introduction to General Relativity, Black Holes, and Cosmology (Oxford, 2015), Chapter IX: Relativistic fluids
sources.locator: Full 300-page book PDF inspected; Chapter IX, printed pp. 208–240, with §§IX.4.1, IX.7.1–IX.7.2, IX.8.1–IX.8.2, IX.9.1, IX.13.1–IX.13.3 and IX.14 read in full. Relevant sections cover the perfect-fluid stress, Euler/entropy hyperbolicity, Einstein–Euler constraints and evolution, barotropic enthalpy, charged-fluid equations, zero versus finite conductivity, and ideal MHD.

contents.name: IX.4.1 Stress–energy tensor of a perfect fluid
contents.support: The chapter supplies an independent perfect-fluid stress formulation. The local definition fixes its own −+++ tensor convention and explicitly separates this fluid tensor from the Maxwell stress supplied by the planned CP01 definition.

contents.name: IX.7.1 Euler and entropy equations as a Leray hyperbolic system
contents.support: The chapter checks the strict sound-speed regime for fluid hyperbolicity. Its third-order Leray formulation is not used as the local proof: the item derives the actual first-order symmetric block and the independent advected-charge block.

contents.name: IX.8.1–IX.8.2 Initial data and evolution for the coupled Einstein–Euler–entropy system
contents.support: The chapter supplies an independent account of the coupled constraint/evolution structure. Its uncharged perfect-fluid system does not establish the sourced Maxwell-fluid theorem; the local proof checks the electromagnetic source, both constraint families and total-stress conservation separately.

contents.name: IX.9.1 Barotropic dynamical velocity and the fluid index
contents.support: The barotropic enthalpy change of variable is relevant to the positive principal matrix. The item defines its own dimensionless variable r and proves its derivative and invertibility under ε+p>0 and 0<p′<1.

contents.name: IX.13.1 Equations for charged perfect fluids
contents.support: The chapter independently records the Lorentz-force balance, Maxwell coupling and current conservation issue. The item derives div j=0 from its exact EOS-defined N and advected Z instead of importing a separately assigned continuity law.

contents.name: IX.13.2 Zero-conductivity charged fluids
contents.support: The zero-conductivity branch is the closest source comparison. The definition selects a purely convective current j=cNZ u and states the advected charge law explicitly; it does not assume the book's thermodynamic entropy construction.

contents.name: IX.13.3 Finite-conductivity charged fluids
contents.reason: The assigned strict branch has no Ohmic conduction current, entropy production or finite-conductivity law; these equations have a different principal system and are deliberately outside its claimed development.

contents.name: IX.14 Ideal magnetohydrodynamics and the infinite-conductivity limit
contents.reason: The assigned model retains a general Maxwell two-form and a convective charge current; it does not impose the ideal-MHD infinite-conductivity constraint or its reduced electromagnetic variables.

sources.title: Daniela Pugliese and Juan A. Valiente Kroon, On the evolution equations for ideal magnetohydrodynamics in curved spacetime, arXiv:1112.1525v1 (2011)
sources.locator: Full 25-page PDF inspected; §§1, 3, 4.1–4.6 and Appendix A read, especially the charged-fluid stress/current equations (16)–(59), the symmetric first-order evolution system (118)–(138), and the explicit constraint-propagation caveat at p. 20; §4.7 on ideal MHD was checked for scope.

contents.name: §3 Einstein–Maxwell–Euler equations, perfect-fluid stress and current split (16)–(59)
contents.support: The article provides a second independent curved-spacetime treatment of charged-fluid stress, Maxwell coupling and the fluid-frame current. Its signature and conductivity variables differ; the local definition fixes its own conventions and uses no conduction term.

contents.name: §3 particle-number and entropy equations (56)–(59), and Appendix A on homentropic/barotropic equations of state
contents.support: The independent derivation confirms why a particle-number balance must accompany the stress equation. The item proves its selected balance from the charged-fluid energy equation and N′=N/(ε+p), then adds the separately adopted advected scalar Z.

contents.name: §4.1–§4.6 first-order symmetric hyperbolic Einstein–Maxwell–Euler reduction and local evolution (118)–(138)
contents.support: This full comparison confirms that the coupled system needs an explicit symmetric reduction. Its Lagrangian tetrad system adds Weyl and ∇F variables and its p. 20 discussion omits constraint propagation; neither is used as a proved supplier. The local proof supplies its own block matrix and checks Maxwell and Einstein subsidiaries.

contents.name: §4.7 Infinitely conductive plasma / ideal MHD
contents.reason: The assigned theorem neither sets the fluid-frame electric field to zero nor takes infinite conductivity; the full field-strength Maxwell block is retained.
